subject: Next steps: Hosted -> Private deployment qualification & regulatory drivers
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Katrina Lopez <katrina.lopez@cardionova.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@cardionova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted -> Private qualification: call recap and immediate asks

Hi Katrina / Michael — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key pain points you called out:
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI within EU-controlled network and a possible future air-gap for audit periods.
- Need for customer-managed KMS/HSM and strict key rotation + audit logs.
- Concerns about cross-border egress and third-party backups.
- Peak inference latency requirement for triage workflows: P95 < 300ms for 256-token requests.

Goals you confirmed:
- PoC on private deployment inside their Frankfurt VPC in Q1 2027.
- Minimal production downtime and documented runbook for failover to hosted fallback.
- Procurement wants an NDA + SOW draft and estimated cost envelope for dedicated capacity vs private install.

Immediate asks / owners:
1) CardioNova: share network diagram, egress rules, and IP allowlist for firewall testing (Katrina) — due 2026-12-04.
2) CardioNova: completed security questionnaire (we requested SOC2 report, current KMS provider) — security@cardionova.com.
3) Redwood: draft SOW scope + high-level runbook and proposed PoC timeline (Hannah) — target 2026-12-03.
4) Redwood Infra: initial compatibility check for HSM/KMS and recommended instance sizing (Ben) — target 2026-12-06.

Attachments I will circulate in the next email: preliminary SOW skeleton and our private-hosting checklist.

If anything above looks off, please flag. Otherwise I'll send the SOW skeleton by EOD and propose a 60-min follow-up the week of Dec 6 for ops deep-dive.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: sow-scope-draft-v1.docx (DOCX, 48 KB))
From: Katrina Lopez <katrina.lopez@cardionova.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@cardionova.com>, security@cardionova.com
Date: 2026-12-01T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Private qualification: call recap and immediate asks

Thanks Hannah — quick confirmation and a few notes.

We agree with your summary. A couple clarifications:
- The air-gap is not continuous; it's a quarterly snapshot process where we want the option to sever external connectivity for a 72-hour attest window.
- We run Vault-backed HSM (HashiCorp Vault + CloudHSM) today; procurement will need a clear integration pattern.
- SOC2 report is available but needs a redaction step; I'll send controlled access to the report.

Files attached: security questionnaire (partial), our simplified network diagram, and a list of point-of-contact emails for NetOps and Security.
(attachment: cardionova-security-qa.xlsx (Excel, 82 KB))
(attachment: network-diagram-CardioNova.pdf (PDF, 210 KB))

We can confirm the network owners will be available for the ops deep-dive on Dec 8 or Dec 9; prefer the 9th afternoon CET.

Katrina Lopez
Head of IT Infrastructure, CardioNova
katrina.lopez@cardionova.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Private qualification: call recap and immediate asks

On Dec 1, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Key pain points you called out:
> - Regulatory requirement to keep PHI within EU-controlled network and a possible future air-gap for audit periods.
> - Need for customer-managed KMS/HSM and strict key rotation + audit logs.

Thanks for the recap — I reviewed Katrina's attachments. Quick notes from infra:
- HSM pattern looks feasible; we need the exact Vault version and current CloudHSM instance type. I'll ping infra to validate kernel/driver compatibility.
- Latency target is tight but achievable with local GPU pools; we should propose an initial cluster of 2x A10G-equivalent for PoC and include a routable fallback to Redwood-hosted for burst (optional).

I'll take ownership of the compatibility check and a short tech appendix for the SOW. Laura, can you loop in procurement/legal for NDA + initial pricing guardrails?

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Private qualification: call recap and immediate asks

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments, Katrina. Next concrete steps from Redwood:

1) SOW skeleton + proposed PoC timeline attached (sow-scope-draft-v1.docx). Expecting review comments by 2026-12-07.
2) Ben will deliver infra compatibility appendix and HSM integration notes by 2026-12-06.
3) Please confirm firewall allowlist / egress IPs and NetOps POC contact by 2026-12-04 so we can schedule network tests the week of Dec 13.
4) Proposed ops deep-dive: Dec 9 at 15:00 CET (Dec 9, 06:00 PST) — I sent a calendar hold separately.

We will also provide a short security evidence binder (SOC2 access + audit log examples) under controlled access once you confirm recipients.

If that aligns, I'll convert the SOW skeleton into a draft SOW for legal to review and include pricing brackets for Dedicated vs Private install.

Thanks — looking forward to the Dec 9 ops deep-dive.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
